pipelines.title: Ping-pong: draft and critique
pipelines.description: Two agents hand one piece of work back and forth. The drafter writes, the critic answers with notes, and the notes go back to the drafter as the next round's brief. The loop is capped at three rounds, so the work cannot circle for ever; when the cap is reached the critic's notes stand as the verdict.

roles.name: Drafter
roles.remit: Write the draft, then rewrite it against the critic's notes.
roles.instructions: Write the draft in one pass and name what you are unsure of. On a later round, rewrite against the critic's notes line by line: a note you disagree with is answered in the draft, not ignored. Stop when the critic accepts the draft or the round cap is reached.

roles.name: Critic
roles.remit: Read the draft against the brief and return notes, never a rewrite.
roles.instructions: Read the draft against the brief. One note per defect, each naming the sentence and the fix it needs. Do not rewrite the draft yourself; your notes are the next round's brief. Accept only when no note is left open. The brief's own text decides the word budget: never invent a ceiling, and treat 4,000 words as a runaway guard rather than a style rule.

stages.title: Draft
stages.purpose: Write the first version of the piece, and every version after it.
stages.prompt: Write the draft the brief asks for, in one pass, and name in a closing line what you are unsure of. On a later round the draft is rewritten against the critic's notes: a note you disagree with is answered in the draft itself, never ignored. Commit the draft on the branch.

stages.title: Critique
stages.purpose: Read the draft against the brief and return one note per defect.
stages.prompt: Read the draft against the brief and return one note per defect: the sentence, the defect, the fix it needs. Do not rewrite the draft. When no note is left open, accept it in one line and record that verdict where the gate asks for it, so the drafter can be told the round is over instead of writing another one. The notes are the artifact the next round reads. The word budget is the brief's own text: enforce the range or ceiling the brief states, and where it states none there is no default ceiling - do not invent one. 4,000 words is the panel's runaway guard rather than a style rule: past it, say the work has run away instead of cutting it to fit.

non: the drafter's notes from another round

handoffs.note: the draft is the critic's only input
the notes are the next round's brief; after three rounds the notes stand as the verdict

gates.name: Verdict
gates.refuses_when: a note is open and the draft was not rewritten against it

pipelines.title: Probe, then fix
pipelines.description: Two stages, and the first one is evidence. The prober reproduces the fault and writes down what it really returned; the fixer reads that report and only then changes anything. A fix with no reproduction is refused, because a change nobody can see fail is a guess.

roles.name: Prober
roles.remit: Reproduce the fault and record the evidence.
roles.instructions: Reproduce the fault before anything is changed, and record the command, its output and the failure it shows. If it does not reproduce, say so and stop: that is a result, not a reason to guess.

roles.name: Fixer
roles.remit: Fix the reproduced fault, and only that.
roles.instructions: Read the probe report first. Change only what the reproduction points at, and prove the same command now passes. A change the report does not point at is out of scope, however obvious it looks.

stages.title: Probe
stages.purpose: Reproduce the fault and record what actually happened.
stages.prompt: Reproduce the fault the task names, against this tree as it stands, and record the exact command, its output and the failure it shows in the probe report. If it does not reproduce, say so in the report and stop — that is the answer, not a reason to guess at one.

stages.title: Fix
stages.purpose: Close the reproduced fault and re-run the same command.
stages.prompt: Read the probe report, then change only what its reproduction points at. Re-run the same command and paste its output into the report as the proof. A change the report does not point at is out of scope; raise it instead of making it.

handoffs.note: the report is the fix's brief and its proof

pipelines.title: Author, review, revise
pipelines.description: Three stages with a capped reject edge. The author writes, the reviewer accepts or rejects, and a rejection returns the manuscript to the author — twice at most. An accepted manuscript goes on to the revision stage, which applies the reviewer's accepted notes as changes rather than as a rewrite.

roles.name: Author
roles.remit: Write the manuscript, and rewrite it after a rejection.
roles.instructions: Write the manuscript in one pass. On a rejection, change what the reviewer's notes name and answer the rest in one line each. Do not rewrite what was accepted: a rejection is a list, not a licence to start again.

roles.name: Reviewer
roles.remit: Accept or reject the manuscript, with notes for each.
roles.instructions: Read the manuscript against the brief and decide: accept, or reject with one note per defect. A rejection must name every defect it counts, because the author can only fix what you wrote down. Do not edit the manuscript.

roles.name: Reviser
roles.remit: Apply the accepted notes as changes.
roles.instructions: Apply the reviewer's accepted notes to the manuscript as changes. Do not add material the notes do not ask for, and do not re-litigate a decision the reviewer already made.

stages.title: Author
stages.purpose: Write the manuscript, and every rewrite after a rejection.
stages.prompt: Write the manuscript the brief asks for, in one pass, and commit it on the branch. When a rejection comes back, change exactly what the reviewer's notes name and answer the rest in one line each; do not rewrite what was accepted.

stages.title: Review
stages.purpose: Accept the manuscript, or reject it with one note per defect.
stages.prompt: Read the manuscript against the brief and decide. Accept it in one line, or reject it with one note per defect: the sentence, the defect, the fix it needs. A rejection names every defect it counts; the author can only fix what you wrote down. Do not edit the manuscript.

stages.title: Revise
stages.purpose: Apply the accepted notes as changes to the accepted manuscript.
stages.prompt: Apply the reviewer's accepted notes to the manuscript as changes, and commit them. Add nothing the notes do not ask for, and do not re-open a decision the reviewer already made. Finish with the acceptance line from the review and the diff that carries it.

non: a rewrite of the accepted text

handoffs.note: the manuscript is what the reviewer decides on
a rejection returns the manuscript to the author with the notes
an acceptance hands the notes on to the reviser

gates.name: Accept or reject
gates.refuses_when: a rejection carries no note, or an acceptance leaves a note open

stages.purpose: The worker opens one pull request and reads it back before reporting it.
stages.prompt:
Open ONE pull request from this tree's branch into the main branch and read it back before reporting it:

  gh pr create --fill

When this branch carries a version bump, --fill drops the reason the bump gave, so pass --title and --body-file instead and put the level and its reason into the body. Then run `gh pr view <n> --json state,headRefOid,baseRefName` and confirm headRefOid is the commit you just pushed. Report the PR URL.

stages.prompt:

--admin is the ruleset's bypass, not a preference: the repository's ruleset, "Owner only" (id 25783530, docs/pushing-to-a-remote.md gate 8), refuses an update to the default branch except through a bypass. --rebase keeps the main branch linear, which the ruleset requires; --merge would be refused.

pipelines.title: SEFL review loop
pipelines.description: Cut a correctly named turnover branch, open a PR for code_review_java, answer what arrives, merge when approved.

roles.name: Worker
roles.remit: Do the work the stage names, in this tree, and commit it.
roles.instructions: Work in this tree and commit what you changed in one revertable commit. Report the files you touched, the commands you ran and their real results. Never push the main branch and never open a pull request unless the stage's own prompt says to.

roles.name: Reviewer
roles.remit: Read the pull request at its current head and approve it, or say what has to change.
roles.instructions: Read the pull request at the head it is now on. An approval at an older commit is not an approval of the head: after any push the head needs re-approval. Approve only when nothing is left open.

stages.title: Name the branch
stages.purpose: The worker renames this tree's branch to the turnover pattern and reports the new name.
stages.prompt: Rename this tree's branch to YYYYMMDD_HHMM_<TICKET>_<desc> and nothing else: the cut's own local time, the ticket id the work names, and <desc> as lowercase words joined by underscores. Example: 20261102_1431_ABC-1234_fix_login_redirect. Then report the new name.

non: a branch name that does not carry the ticket

stages.title: Push the branch
stages.purpose: The worker pushes this tree's branch to origin and never the main branch.
stages.prompt: Push the branch, never the main branch: git push origin HEAD. If the push is refused, report the refusal and stop — the panel's permission box is the only thing that grants a write.

non: a push to the main branch

stages.title: Open the pull request
stages.purpose: The worker opens one pull request for code_review_java and reads it back.
stages.prompt:
Open ONE pull request from this tree's branch into the main branch on the project's host, following the landing doctrine exactly:

- title: "Java Code Review for <repo> <branch>"
- reviewers: the GROUP code_review_java and nothing else — no individuals, no DAL group on a non-DAL change
- description, four sections, every one present: ## Jira Ticket, ## Description, ## Test Procedures, ## Technical Specifications

POST it to the host's pull-request endpoint with the landing doctrine's REST path and bearer token, fromRef refs/heads/<the branch you pushed>, toRef refs/heads/<the main branch>. Read the PR back: reviewers must be exactly [code_review_java], and fromRef.latestCommit must be the head you pushed. Report the PR id and URL.

stages.title: Wait for the reviewer
stages.purpose: The worker reads the pull request's activities once and ends the turn, and the panel re-checks on its own clock.
stages.prompt: Read the PR's activities once (the landing doctrine names the endpoint). Report what arrived, then END the turn: say plainly that nothing has arrived if nothing has. Do not sleep, do not poll in a loop, and do not merge — the panel re-checks on its own clock and wakes this thread when there is something to answer.

stages.title: Answer the review
stages.purpose: The worker answers each new comment with the smallest change, commits it, pushes and replies naming the commit.
stages.prompt: For each new comment on the PR for this tree's branch: make the smallest change that answers it, commit on this tree's branch, push, and reply on that comment naming the commit. Then report what you answered. An approval at an older commit is not an approval of the head — after any push the head needs re-approval.

non: a change no comment asked for

stages.title: Wait for the approval at the head
stages.purpose: The reviewer approves the pull request at its current head, and the worker reports the reviewer and the commit.
stages.prompt: Nothing to say: wait for the head to be reviewed. The stage ends when an approval exists whose lastReviewedCommit equals the PR's current head. Report the reviewer and the commit they approved.

non: an approval at an older commit

stages.title: Merge
stages.purpose: The worker merges the pull request at its current version and confirms the main branch moved.
stages.prompt: Merge the PR for this tree's branch with its current version: POST the host's merge endpoint (the landing doctrine names it) with the PR id and ?version=<the PR's current version>. Then confirm the main branch moved. Never push the main branch directly and never decline or close the PR.

non: a direct push to the main branch
a declined or closed pull request
